item: a committing restore refuses while a registered background job that writes to the corpus runs, naming it (R659, OPEN_QUEUE item 21 option B reduced); item 18 closed as a stated limit with a guard (R660)
summary: BEFORE: the restore's exclusive window stopped only the collection loop and Run now; a registered background job that commits to the corpus (the governments loads, tag backfills, language detection, source qualification, the mailbox pull...) kept writing, and everything it committed between the working copy and the swap was discarded by the swap, silently. The task manager's 'another job is writing' ask read a second, hand-kept list (_DB_WRITER_KINDS) that named 6 of the 19 registered writer kinds. NOW: running_writer_jobs() in src/jobs/background.py reads the registry's own is_writer flags (one list). refuse_while_writer_jobs_run() in src/backup/merge.py raises WriterJobsRefused (a RestoreRefused) naming the running writers by label, with nothing imported and nothing written: before the backup is decrypted or staged (the volume restore; the single-file restore once the file is read), before run_restore prepares anything, and again at the working copy; a preview is never refused. A job whose stop loses nothing (the new stops_for_restore flag, cancellable jobs only, set only on reindex-resume, which resumes from its watermark and which the import starts again) is asked to step aside (ctx.yielding, a yield the drain reports as paused for the import, never the operator's cancel), one 30 s wait for all, and named only if it still runs; the writers it may not stop are read FIRST, so a restore that will refuse anyway stops nothing. Whatever the restore's outcome, its end starts the stopped jobs again (start_jobs_stopped_for_restore, in the volume and single-file restores' finally and on a refusal; inside an import run's window the run starts the drain once at its end). The run journal records the refusal under its own reason (writer-jobs), not the swap barrier's. /api/jobs carries import_refused (the refusal the server would raise now, read without stopping anything), and the import page shows it, for an import holding a corpus or legacy backup (large data and newsletters alone are never refused), instead of offering 'Start anyway?' for an import the server would refuse; db_writers_busy/busy_with now join the hand-kept kinds with every registry writer. The refusal is a fixed English sentence the page turns into the operator's language (ooServerText, the job labels translated where the page has them), keyed in all 12 locales; it says 'let it finish, or stop it if it can be stopped', since some writers cannot be cancelled. tests/test_restore_refuses_writer_jobs.py (13 tests, red on main: the functions, the flag, the class, the field and the refusal did not exist). R660: OPEN_QUEUE item 18 / R338 R340 closes as the stated limit written in tests/test_repair_probe_parked_writer.py's docstring, and test_every_raw_write_lock_transaction_in_src_is_classified pins every literal BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE a statement in src/ issues (6 files, 16 statements, each with why it cannot hold SQLite's lock across the repair's window). That guard sees only that spelling: a write lock taken by engine.begin(), exec_driver_sql, a plain BEGIN or a raw sqlite3 implicit transaction passes it, as does a site moving inside a pinned file (stated in the docstring). Stated limits: a job started after the working copy is not caught; writers that are not registry jobs (the collection pass, the housekeeping lane, the Wikipedia drain, API write routes, the newsletter and source deletions) and writers left unflagged on purpose (tests/test_job_writer_flags.py) are outside the list; jobs that cannot be stopped refuse an import until they end, and the indexes a fresh launch builds (title-index, keyword-day-counts) refuse one until they are done or stopped; in a checkpoint group a refusal at a later item discards the merges the group still held, as any refusal there does; a legacy item inside the import queue shows the refusal in English, since the queue prefixes its status code to the text (as it already does for the wrong-passphrase sentence). Release-notes line: «An import now refuses to start while a background job is writing to your corpus, and names the job, instead of silently discarding what that job writes during the import. A re-index still finishing from an earlier import is paused for the import and picked up again afterwards.»
